title: Agentic AI Reliability Testing Harness: Asymmetric Trust Boundaries, Five Structural Evaluation Levels, PEP Gateways, Behavioral Invariants, and Three-State Release Gates
author: Vasuki Uday Kiran Vudathala (freeCodeCamp.org, 2026; synthesized by Brain Harness)

source.title: Agentic AI Reliability: Build a Testing Harness for Tool Use, Guardrails, Loops, & Workflow Outcomes [Full Book]

claims.assertion: A polite, fluent conversational response is not evidence that an agentic workflow succeeded; outcome correctness must be verified directly from authoritative world state, completely independent of the agent's narration.
claims.source: Vasuki Uday Kiran Vudathala: 'The Demo That Lied' & Chapter 1 (2026)

claims.assertion: Evaluation requires two distinct orthogonal taxonomies: Six Evaluation Activities (when and why evidence is gathered) and Five Evaluation Levels (what structural component of an execution is judged: Response, Step, Action, Workflow, System).

The agent must never supply its own identity, tenant, or scopes; SecurityContext must be bound to the Policy Enforcement Point (PEP) Gateway at request initialization, and the gateway must fail closed.

Safety guardrail evaluation must distinguish four discrete outcomes: pass (control blocked forbidden action), fail/bypass (control breached), not_exercised (action never attempted), and indeterminate.

Release gates must be three-state (pass, fail, inconclusive); missing or ambiguous telemetry must block releases without dishonesty, and critical safety metrics must enforce the Rule of Three upper bound with zero observed false successes under fault.
